daily_compact_mode.summary: Under the cost-saving daily-compact operating mode (config/scheduled_tasks.json -> operating_mode), weekday tasks suppress no-op / heartbeat notifications and notify ONLY for actionable events. Heavy narrative reporting is deferred to the Friday 5:00 PM ET weekly refresh.
actionable_events: blocked signal-generation entry point (GATE5_DISABLED, seven-slot Claude roster)
daily_compact_mode.actionable_events_note_2026_07_30: GATE5_DISABLED was added as an explicit actionable event on 2026-07-30 alongside claude/dca-executor-prompts/*.txt's Gate 5/Gate 9 alerting fix: that verdict is a known, expected gap (no signal-generation entry point exists yet, see PRODUCTION_READINESS.md) rather than an error in the traditional sense, so it did not already match any entry on this list -- without this addition, an agent following this policy literally could still treat the new Gate 5 alert as a routine/heartbeat notification and suppress it, reproducing the exact silent-executor problem the prompt change was meant to fix (see PRODUCTION_READINESS.md). GATE4_EXPECTED_OVERLAP was added the same day for the same reason: it is likewise a known, expected condition (Gate 4 recognizing the legacy stream's own same-window order) rather than a traditional error, so an agent honoring suppress_no_op_notifications could otherwise discard it as a no-op -- but the 10:30/12:30/3:30 prompts now require all three Gate 9 channels for it too, same as GATE5_DISABLED.

slack.note: The in-app message center is the primary notification channel, not Slack. No routine run confirmations, dashboards, or heartbeats are ever posted to Slack. The ONLY two Slack paths anywhere in this project are the opt-in, off-by-default webhooks below (drift and failure alerts); both stay silent unless an operator explicitly sets their env var.

optional_drift_alert.purpose: Opt-in path for immediate drift alerts from scripts/drift_detection.py only.
optional_drift_alert.secret_policy: The webhook URL is read from the DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK environment variable (or --slack-webhook) at runtime and is NEVER stored in git or this config. Leave the env var unset to keep Slack off; the detector then falls back to in_app_message_center routing.
optional_drift_alert.enable: Set DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK in the scheduler environment and pass --slack to the detector.

optional_failure_alert.purpose: Opt-in path for uncaught-exception failure alerts from dca_alerts.py's shared entrypoint wrapper only (any live stream's run crashing with an unhandled exception), not for routine run outcomes.
optional_failure_alert.secret_policy: The webhook URL is read from DCA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK (falling back to DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK if unset) at runtime and is NEVER stored in git or this config. Leave both env vars unset to keep Slack off; a broken/unreachable webhook never masks or blocks the underlying failure handling (logging, heartbeat, failed-start marker) per dca_alerts.py.
optional_failure_alert.enable: Set DCA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK (or reuse DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK) in the scheduler environment.

optional_watchdog_alert.purpose: Opt-in path for scripts/schedule_watchdog.py only: an independent, non-LLM-judgment check that a live slot left valid scheduled evidence. Added 2026-09-25 because every other channel (in-app message center, the Gate 9 repo alert file, email) is written BY the executor session, so a session that ends on a question instead of following the abort-and-alert rule (see docs/safeguards.md's live execution roster note) leaves silence on all three -- recorded 2026-09-14, 09-15, 09-17, 09-22 x2, 09-25.
optional_watchdog_alert.secret_policy: The webhook URL is read from DCA_WATCHDOG_SLACK_WEBHOOK (falling back to DCA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK, then DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK if unset) at runtime and is NEVER stored in git or this config. Leave all three env vars unset to keep Slack off; the watchdog's own idempotent, durable repo alert file (write_watchdog_alert_files, under schedule_watchdog/alerts/) and its non-zero exit code are unaffected either way.
optional_watchdog_alert.enable: Set DCA_WATCHDOG_SLACK_WEBHOOK (or reuse DCA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK / DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK) in the environment scripts/schedule_watchdog.py runs under. See docs/schedule_verification.md#watchdog-alerting-independently-of-the-executor-session-2026-09-25.

email.scope: Only where a task explicitly says to email; no routine dashboard emails.

routing_conditions.gate5_disabled_alerts: Added 2026-07-30, when GATE5_DISABLED (the seven-slot Claude roster's blocked-entry-point verdict, see PRODUCTION_READINESS.md) became an actionable, alerting event: each executor prompt's Gate 9 requires all three of IN-APP MESSAGE CENTER, REPO ALERT FILE, and EMAIL for that verdict specifically. That third channel read EMAIL DRAFT until 2026-08-26, on the mistaken premise that the connector could not send; every prompt now requires the email to be SENT, with a draft permitted only as a fallback -- either where the connector genuinely exposes no send capability, or where a send is attempted and fails (auth, throttling, provider or network errors) -- and in either case the executor says so in the primary alert (see docs/alert_digest.md for the ~50 undelivered drafts the narrower wording produced). Deliberately a SEPARATE route from live_run_alerts, not a widening of it: live_run_alerts is shared by every live-run alert category, including the five currently-live legacy tasks, and channels.email.scope/docs/safeguards.md are explicit that email is sent only where a task explicitly requests it -- unconditionally adding email to the shared route would have emailed on every legacy live-run alert too, not just this one verdict. The REPO ALERT FILE channel is not one of this file's three channels (slack/in_app_message_center/email) and is not routed through this table at all -- it is written directly by the executor to dca_paths.stream_root(...) as described in each prompt's Gate 9, a durable-fallback mechanism this config has no representation for.
routing_conditions.gate4_expected_overlap_alerts: Added 2026-07-30 (same day as gate5_disabled_alerts), when GATE4_EXPECTED_OVERLAP -- the 10:30/12:30/3:30 Claude slots' classification for a same-window order recognized as the legacy morning-dca-/midday-dca-/graded-dca- stream, not a rogue second executor -- stopped ending those fires silently. Mirrors gate5_disabled_alerts exactly: a SEPARATE route from live_run_alerts for the same email-scoping reason (channels.email.scope/docs/safeguards.md), and the REPO ALERT FILE channel is likewise written directly by the executor per Gate 9, not represented in this table.
routing_conditions.capital_priority_briefing: Notify (in-app + email) only if at least one ticker triggers a 1.5x or higher multiplier; otherwise silent.
routing_conditions.premarket_buying_power: Analytics dashboard only; no routine notification.
routing_conditions.volatility_outliers: Alert only for >5% outliers or actionable errors.
routing_conditions.drift_alerts: Fire an IMMEDIATE alert when scripts/drift_detection.py detects an auto-buy signal (auto_buy_signal true and incremental_order_amount > 0 or desired amount > 0) with no corresponding submitted-order record. Routes to in_app_message_center by default; also posts to Slack when DCA_DRIFT_SLACK_WEBHOOK is set and the detector is run with --slack. Never routine/heartbeat -- only on detected drift.
routing_conditions.watchdog_alerts: Added 2026-09-25 for scripts/schedule_watchdog.py: fires when a live roster slot left no valid scheduled evidence, independently of whether the executor session for that slot alerted on its own (see channels.slack.optional_watchdog_alert and docs/schedule_verification.md's watchdog section). This is the one alert category not produced by an executor session at all, so 'in_app_message_center' here means whatever invokes the watchdog on its own schedule relays its result there -- the script itself cannot post to it. Always writes its own idempotent, durable repo alert file (write_watchdog_alert_files, under schedule_watchdog/alerts/, a distinct root from every executor stream's own alerts/ directory, overwriting rather than numbering a repeat fire for the same still-unresolved day/slot) regardless of Slack configuration; also posts to Slack when DCA_WATCHDOG_SLACK_WEBHOOK (or a fallback) is set and the watchdog is run with --slack. Never routine -- only when scripts.verify_schedule.verify_day reports a slot outside OK_STATUSES.
routing_conditions.month_end_volatility_risk: Month-end volatility risk refresh (tasks c9fb1fb8/17a3b2a9, see month_end_volatility_risk_policy in config/scheduled_tasks.json). Notify (in-app + email) ONLY if the Notion refresh fails, data quality blocks the run, or one or more tickers triggered the 3x tier more than twice; otherwise silent. Email subject: 'Month-end DCA volatility risk table'. No Slack. The run also ends silently with no notification when the final-eligible-market-day gate does not pass.
routing_conditions.daily_compact_mode: Weekday daily tasks suppress no-op/heartbeat notifications and notify only for the actionable events listed in daily_compact_mode.actionable_events (placed/rejected orders, budget-capped candidates, missing/invalid artifacts, broker/log mismatch, data-confidence failures, drift-detector failures, recovery attempts/failures, meaningful exceptions, blocked signal-generation entry point / GATE5_DISABLED for the seven-slot Claude roster, expected legacy-stream overlap / GATE4_EXPECTED_OVERLAP for the 10:30/12:30/3:30 Claude slots). Full narrative/dashboard reporting is deferred to the Friday weekly refresh (041d9d90).
